title: O2 Project
subtitle: Development concept, brand positioning, and capital-preparation materials for an urban mixed-use destination project.
summary: The O2 folder reads as a live development and positioning archive: renders, floor-by-floor planning, tower studies, brand guidelines, pitch materials, and a pro forma. This portfolio version turns that archive into a coherent public case shell anchored by visuals while preserving raw development and finance documents as restricted source artifacts.

kpis.label: Core planning files
kpis.subtext: Development, flooring, blocking, and TIF materials

kpiSummary.budget: Concept-to-capital-preparation archive spanning design narrative, development studies, branding, and TIF-oriented financial support materials.
kpiSummary.rates: No formal fee sheet was included in this folder, so this portfolio entry is framed around deliverable depth and project-preparation scope rather than contract economics.
kpiSummary.outcomes: Demonstrates the ability to package a place-based development concept through renders, planning documentation, pitch materials, and financial scaffolding in a way investors and partners can understand.
challenges: The archive contains strong visual and strategic materials but no ready-made case-study narrative, so the portfolio entry must be assembled from the deliverables themselves.
Development story, brand story, and capital story all need to stay coherent across different document types.
Several of the strongest source files are finance and planning documents that should stay restricted until preview-safe extracts are created.

carousel.title: 1. Overview
carousel.heading: A concept archive becoming a public-facing case
carousel.content: The O2 materials show a development project being shaped across renders, brand positioning, pitch collateral, planning files, and a developer-oriented financial model.

carousel.title: 2. Situation
carousel.heading: Strong assets, but no single portfolio narrative yet
carousel.content: The folder contains rich source material, but the work needs a clear public structure to explain what the project is and why the deliverables matter.

carousel.title: 3. The Ask
carousel.heading: Turn development materials into an investable story
carousel.content: That means presenting the place, the brand, the design intent, and the capital-preparation logic as one coherent package.

carousel.title: 4. The Approach
carousel.heading: Lead with image, support with planning logic
carousel.content: The public version anchors on renders and destination imagery while the floor studies, TIF letters, and pro forma remain visible in the data model as restricted supporting artifacts.

carousel.title: 5. The Work
carousel.heading: Renders, deck, development files, and pro forma
carousel.content: The deliverable set includes visual concept renders, pitch materials, floor-by-floor and tower studies, brand guidelines, and a developer pro forma workbook.

carousel.title: 6. Results
carousel.heading: A credible development-positioning package
carousel.content: Even without a single summary memo, the archive proves concept packaging depth across design, narrative, and early capital-preparation materials.

carousel.title: 7. Selected artifacts
carousel.heading: Visual-first public proof with restricted technical files
carousel.content: This portfolio entry uses renders and site imagery for public viewing while documenting the deeper development files as restricted structured artifacts.
